subject: chemistry
pass: wave3 expert pass (Sonnet-equivalent CUET expert review, same procedure as waves 1 and 2)
scope: All 69 accepted chemistry questions of wave3-candidates-scored-2026-10-17.json (all 69 engine-eligible in wave3-engine-check-working-2026-10-17.json). Every question was solved independently first; then key, explanation, options (length and grammar giveaways, wrong-direction traps), unit and chapter against data/nta_blueprints/chemistry.json, ncert_ref, CUET level and time were checked. NCERT itself was not available (no network); the NCERT check is against the reviewer's knowledge of the current Class 12 Chemistry books (rationalised numbering: Part I Ch 1 to 5, Part II Ch 6 to 10). No model call, database or network was used.
notes: Verdict "drop" is the wave-3 equivalent of wave 2 practice or reject: not publishable.

Systemic: 36 refs only needed a text-only ncert_ref fix (plus the repaired items that also have one): the chapter number and Part matched no single NCERT edition (Electrochemistry as Part I Ch 3, d- and f-Block as Part II Ch 4, Aldehydes Ch 12, Amines Ch 13, Biomolecules Ch 14). None of them changes what a solver sees. ncert_ref is in the content hash, so these need the same admit-on-expert-verdict treatment as the wave 2 explanation-only repairs.

Five repairs change solver-visible text (ids in solver_visible_text_changed: one stem name, four option sets). Under the wave-1 rule they need a fresh blind re-solve; under the wave-2 rule for text-only repairs they do not. The reviewer re-solved each and the key is unchanged.

Key position of the 69 questions: A 16, B 17, C 18, D 18. The key was the unique longest option in 13 of 56 single-choice items before repair; the four large-margin cases (7c42a42d, d8db492b, 2b8ad4d9, 8ead33c1) are repaired.

verdicts.why: Solved: the longest chain through C-OH has four carbons, OH gets locant 2, methyl on C-3, so 3-methylbutan-2-ol. Key A correct and unique; B and D are the wrong-numbering traps. Unit and chapter match the blueprint.

Tertiary alcohol (2-methylpropan-2-ol) gives immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent at room temperature; butan-2-ol is slow, the two primary alcohols give none. Key D correct and unique. Explanation sound.

Hydroboration-oxidation of propene is anti-Markovnikov and gives propan-1-ol. Key C correct; propan-2-ol is the acid-hydration trap that the explanation names. NCERT Ch 7 treats exactly this reaction.
Acidity order phenol (pKa about 10) > water > ethanol, cyclohexanol, so phenol. Key C correct and unique. Easy, one-step recall.

Reimer-Tiemann gives salicylaldehyde, Kolbe gives salicylic acid, Williamson (NaOMe + bromoethane) gives methoxyethane, hydroboration-oxidation of propene gives propan-1-ol: B is the only option with all four pairings. Options are true pairings; no position pattern.
Tertiary carbocation, Saytzeff product 2-methylbut-2-ene. Key D correct and unique. Option C (an alkane) is a weak distractor because the stem asks for an alkene, but it does not affect correctness.
EtMgBr + HCHO, then hydrolysis, gives CH3CH2CH2OH, propan-1-ol. Key D correct; propan-2-ol and butan-2-ol need ethanal or propanal. Matches NCERT Grignard route to primary alcohols.

Increasing acidity: ethanol < water < phenol < p-nitrophenol, which is (B), (D), (C), (A). Key B correct. The key is not the listed order (A to D), and option A is the exact reverse, which is the intended trap.
NCERT: 413 K gives diethyl ether and 443 K gives ethene, so I and II are true and III is false. Key D correct. Option text is consistent with the stem statements.

Phenol with bromine water gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol (white precipitate). Key C correct and unique. Option C is longest only because trisubstituted names are longer; the options are names of different compounds, not a prose giveaway.

Chemistry is right: the tertiary side cleaves by SN1, so (CH3)3C-I and CH3OH; key D correct and unique. Defect: the stem name "2-Methyl-2-methoxypropane" is not in IUPAC order (substituents go alphabetically, methoxy before methyl) and this chapter teaches nomenclature.
verdicts.repair: Stem name "2-Methyl-2-methoxypropane" changed to "2-Methoxy-2-methylpropane" (the formula (CH3)3C-O-CH3 is unchanged). Options, key and explanation unchanged. Solver-visible text changed: yes (name only).

verdicts.why: I true (hydrogen bonding, bp 78 C against -24 C), II true, III false (phenol does not liberate CO2 from NaHCO3; NCERT uses this to separate phenols from carboxylic acids). Key C correct.

Tertiary alcohol dehydrates more easily because of the more stable tertiary carbocation; R states that stability and correctly explains A. Key A correct. Option wording is the standard assertion-reason set.

PCC stops at propanal, acidified dichromate takes propan-1-ol to propanoic acid, propan-2-ol gives propanone, hot concentrated H2SO4 turns ethanol to ethene: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV) = B. All four options are real pairings. Key correct and unique.

Boron goes to the less substituted alkene carbon (the CH carbon), OH ends up there: 2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol. Key A correct and unique. The cyclic substrate goes a step past NCERT (propene only) but applies the same anti-Markovnikov rule; hard label fair; answerable in 72 s.

Williamson is SN2, so the tertiary group must sit on the alkoxide and the halide must be methyl: sodium tert-butoxide + iodomethane, key C. Options A and D (tertiary halide) give elimination; B gives dimethyl ether. Key unique.
Acid-catalysed hydration of 2-methylpropene follows Markovnikov via the tertiary cation: 2-methylpropan-2-ol. Key D correct and unique.
2-Chlorobutane has a stereocentre (H, Cl, CH3, C2H5); the other three have none. Key A correct and unique.
SN2 rate falls with crowding: CH3Br > C2H5Br > 2-bromopropane > 2-bromo-2-methylpropane = (B), (D), (C), (A). Key B correct. Not the listed order; option A (listed order) is the tertiary-first trap.
I true (inversion), II true (planar cation, near racemisation), III false (tertiary halides go by SN1 or elimination). Key C correct. Hard label is generous but the item is exam-appropriate.
Alcoholic KOH, Saytzeff: but-2-ene is the major alkene from 2-bromobutane. Key C correct and unique; but-1-ene is the Hofmann minor product.

Finkelstein NaI/acetone, Swarts AgF or Hg2F2, Wurtz Na in dry ether, chlorobenzene + NaOH at about 623 K then acid (the industrial phenol route NCERT describes): (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV) = B. Key correct and unique. The label "Dow process" is common in coaching books rather than NCERT wording, but the list-II description it is paired with is NCERT content, so left as is.
Grignard reagent protonated by water gives the alkane ethane. Key D correct and unique.
